records.title: Trump's Stand for Truth in Big Pharma Ads - AMAC
records.retrieval_query: Search the National Archives archived Trump White House website (2017-2021) transcript pages for the August 27, 2020 remarks and check whether the wording "Last month, I took on Big Pharma" appears verbatim with date and venue.

passages.P4: by AMAC — The Association of Mature American Citizens
passages.P5: President Donald Trump has once again done what few in Washington have dared to do: he’s taken on deceptive and dishonest Big Pharma practices and sided squarely with the American people.
passages.P6: Last month, Trump issued a presidential memorandum directing Health and Human Services Secretary Robert Kennedy, Jr., to require pharmaceutical companies to fully disclose every possible side effect in their direct-to-consumer drug advertisements. While Big Pharma whined that this was a speech control measure, in reality, it is a restoration of basic standards of truth and accountability in advertising. By demanding full transparency, Trump is protecting the public by prohibiting drugmakers from engaging in manipulative marketing.
passages.P7: For nearly three decades, this problem has been growing. In the 1990s, Americans heard the full list of potential side effects every time a new drug was advertised. It wasn’t flattering, but it was honest – and it reminded people that powerful medicine carries real risks.
passages.P8: Then, in 1997, the FDA quietly loosened the rules, allowing companies to cherry-pick a few warnings and direct consumers elsewhere for the fine print. That bureaucratic “streamlining” turned out to be *carte blanche* for Big Pharma to flood American TV screens with emotional, one-sided sales pitches.
passages.P9: And flood they did. Year after year, drug advertising budgets have climbed, surpassing $10 billion last year. Roughly half of that money flowed straight to television networks – a financial lifeline for struggling media companies that bought not just airtime, but influence throughout the entire newsroom.
passages.P10: The voices that once held Big Pharma corporations accountable became dependent on their ad dollars. Any networks that threatened to expose the potential harms of medications risked losing millions from drug companies. Big Pharma began determining the national conversation about health, while everyday Americans were left with only half the truth.
passages.P11: President Trump’s memorandum takes square aim at this corrupt relationship. By reinstating full disclosure rules reminiscent of the 1990s, he’s calling Big Pharma’s bluff. If these companies truly believe in their products, they should have no fear of telling the whole story, side effects and all. If they refuse, it reveals that their ads were really about manipulation, not education. Trump’s message is that honesty is not optional when it comes to public health.
passages.P12: HHS under Kennedy has enthusiastically embraced this new directive. “Pharmaceutical ads hooked this country on prescription drugs,” Kennedy said in a statement. “We will shut down that pipeline of deception and require drug companies to disclose all critical safety facts in their advertising. Only radical transparency will break the cycle of overmedicalization that drives America’s chronic disease epidemic.”
passages.P13: “For far too long, the FDA has permitted misleading drug advertisements, distorting the doctor-patient relationship and creating increased demand for medications regardless of clinical appropriateness,” FDA Commissioner Marty Makary added. “Drug companies spend up to 25 percent of their budget on advertising. Those billions of dollars would be better spent on lowering drug prices for everyday Americans.”

records.title: Archived Presidential White House Websites
records.retrieval_query: Is there a transcript, audio, or video recording from a primary source (such as an official White House transcript or event footage) that contains this statement?

passages.P2: White House websites are Presidential records. The official files that make up a Presidential administration's website are preserved in our Executive Office of the President Electronic Records Archive. In order for the public to easily access the websites, the National Archives has taken an additional step to "freeze" the White House websites and make them available online. Because the archived websites are hosted by the National Archives and are historical material, they are no longer updated. Any broken links (internal or external) will not be updated.
passages.P3: The archived websites are an excellent resource for photographs, speeches, press releases, digital data and other public domain records.
passages.P5: In January 2025, the following website was archived as a way to preserve the online presence of the administration of President Joseph R. Biden Jr.
passages.P6:
* Archived Biden White House Website  
  The archived White House website is a useful resource for photographs, speeches, press releases, and other public domain records of the Biden Presidency from 2021-2025.
passages.P8: In January 2021, the following websites were archived as a way to preserve the online presence of the administration of President Donald J. Trump.
passages.P9:
* Archived Trump White House Website  
  The archived White House website is a useful resource for photographs, speeches, press releases, and other public domain records of the Trump Presidency from 2017-2021.
* Archived Be Best Website  
  The “Be Best” Initiative was developed by First Lady Melania Trump to focus on major issues facing children today. It concentrated on three main pillars: well-being, online safety, and opioid abuse.
* Archived Artificial Intelligence for the American People Website  
  The Artificial Intelligence for the American People website was a resource for those who want to learn more about how to take full advantage of the opportunities of AI.
* Archived Coronavirus Disease 2019 Website  
  The Coronavirus Disease 2019 website is a resource of information related to the COVID-19 pandemic.
* Archived Opioids: the Crisis Next Doors Website  
  The Crisis Next Door website was created as a portal for Americans to share their stories about opioid addiction or recovery.
* Archived Trump White House "We the People" Website  
  The "We the People" site was a platform used during the administration that allowed the public to create a petition online, share it, and collect signatures. According to the website, if a petition gathered 100,000 signatures in 30 days, the White House reviewed the petition and issued an official response.
* Archived Women’s Global Development and Prosperity Initiative Website  
  The Women’s Global Development and Prosperity Initiative was created and led by Ivanka Trump as the first whole-of-government effort to advance global women’s economic empowerment.
passages.P11: In January 2017, the White House websites were archived as a way to preserve the online presence of the administration of President Barack Obama.

  Donald Trump: Maybe I’d run for president. I don’t know.
  + An interview with Rona Barrett (1980)
passages.P9:
* Rona Barrett: Would you like to be the President of the United States?  
  Donald Trump: I really don't believe I would, Rona. But I would like to see somebody as the president who could do the job, and there are very capable people in this country.  
  Barrett: Why wouldn't you dedicate yourself to public service?  
  Trump: Because I think it's a very mean life. I would love, and I would dedicate my life to this country but I see it as being a mean life, and I also see it in somebody with strong views, and somebody with the kind of views that are maybe a little bit unpopular, which may be right, but may be unpopular, wouldn't necessarily have a chance of getting elected against somebody with no great brain but a big smile.

passages.P2: # White House Gov Videos: Official Updates & Inside Look
passages.P7: White House gov videos provide official, on demand access to presidential addresses, policy briefings, and ceremonial events. These recordings serve as a primary source for citizens, journalists, and researchers who want accurate information directly from the government.
passages.P8: Because they are produced by federal agencies, these videos follow strict standards for clarity, accessibility, and archival integrity. Understanding how they are published and indexed helps viewers find the most relevant content quickly.
passages.P9:
| Video Type | Typical Length | Primary Distribution Channel | Accessibility Features |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Presidential Addresses | 5–15 minutes | WhiteHouse.gov, YouTube, C-SPAN | Closed captions, transcripts |
| Press Briefings | 30–90 minutes | WhiteHouse.gov/live, official social feeds | Live captions, archived pages |
| Ceremonial Events | 10–60 minutes | WhiteHouse.gov, official archives | Highlights, full captions |
| Policy Deep Dives | 15–45 minutes | WhiteHouse.gov, agency portals | Summaries, key quotes section |
passages.P10: ## Accessing Official White House Video Archives
passages.P11: The White House website organizes videos by administration, event type, and date, making it easy to locate specific speeches or briefings. Visitors can filter by topic, year, or format to match their needs.
passages.P12: Each video page includes metadata such as the date, location, and related policy documents. This structured approach ensures that users can verify context and cite sources accurately.
passages.P13: ## Key Topics Covered in Official Recordings
passages.P14: White House gov videos span a wide range of subjects, from national security updates to scientific announcements. These recordings capture the official narrative on major initiatives.
passages.P15:
* State of the Union addresses and annual legislative agendas
* Economic updates, budget proposals, and infrastructure plans
* International diplomacy, treaties, and foreign aid announcements
* Public health guidance, emergency responses, and scientific research
passages.P17: Government video production teams follow strict technical guidelines to ensure clarity, stability, and consistency across all recordings. High definition formats are now standard for new uploads.
passages.P18: These standards include frame rate, audio normalization, and color calibration, which help archival footage remain usable for long term reference and broadcast reuse.
passages.P19: ## History and Evolution of Official Government Videography
passages.P20: The history of White House gov videos reflects advances in broadcast technology and public access policies. Early recordings were distributed on physical media, while modern releases prioritize digital streaming.
passages.P21: Milestones include the transition to web based streaming, the adoption of open captioning, and integration with social media platforms that increase reach while maintaining authenticity.
passages.P23: ### Where can I find the most recent official White House videos?
passages.P24: You can find the latest videos on WhiteHouse.gov and its dedicated video portal, which are mirrored on official YouTube and social channels for broader reach.
passages.P25: ### Are these videos captioned and available in multiple languages?
passages.P26: Yes, most new recordings include closed captions in English, and agencies often provide Spanish or additional language versions for key addresses.
